content.body:
Fortunately the development of ever-thicker armor had been foreseen by German gun developers in the prewar years, and the PaK.38 was already nearly finished when the inadequacies of the PaK.36 became apparent. Unfortunately the pace of change exceeded their predictions and the PaK.38, while definitely a more capable weapon, was already outclassed on the battlefield by some heavier tanks ... still unable to easily defeat the frontal armor of the Matilda II, for example.
In every other way it was an outstanding gun being small, low-profile, easy to handle (despite it being rather heavy for its caliber) and incorporating a number of innovative design features.
The PaK.38 is a significant step up from the PaK.36, but still not enough to engage some enemy armor with confidence from all aspects. Its again a very accurate gun, allowing you to aim at very small vulnerable areas from ranges of 750 meters or more.
